blocks.content: You'll build an alert that watches the QuickPizza app for server errors. You'll use Builder mode instead of using a query language.

blocks.title: Select the QuickPizza Prometheus data source

blocks.content: Point the alert rule at the **grafanacloud-play-prom** data source from the QuickPizza tutorial data sources. It's filled in for you.
blocks.tooltip: Prometheus data source from the QuickPizza tutorial data sources.

blocks.content: **Builder** mode lets you construct the query by clicking dropdowns instead of typing PromQL. It's the default for new queries — if **Code** is selected, click **Builder** to switch.

In the **Metric** drop-down, `quickpizza_server_http_requests_total` is filled in for you. This counter tracks every HTTP request QuickPizza's services handle, labeled with the response `status` — the raw material for the alert.
blocks.tooltip: Counter of QuickPizza HTTP requests, broken down by status code.

blocks.content: The raw metric covers *all* requests. To keep only server errors, add a **Label filter** on `status` — it's filled in for you.
Change the operator from `=` to `=~`. The `=~` operator does a regex match, so one filter catches every 5xx code at once (500, 502, 503, and so on).
In the value field, `5..` is filled in for you. That regex matches any three-digit status starting with 5 — so the query now returns only server errors.
The metric is a *counter* that only goes up, so its raw value doesn't tell you whether errors just happened. `increase()` fixes that. Click **+ Operations** to open the picker.
Select **Range functions**, then **Increase**. Set the range to `5m` — the query now counts new errors in the last 5 minutes.

Without `Sum`, you get one number per QuickPizza service — noisier, harder to read. Summing gives one total so the alert answers "is QuickPizza having errors *anywhere*?" Click **+ Operations** again to open the picker.
Select **Aggregations**, then **Sum**. Grafana wraps your `increase()` result in a single total across all services.
Toggle **Explain** on. Grafana narrates what each part of your query does in plain English — a fast way to learn what you're clicking without knowing PromQL syntax.

Click **Run queries** to preview the data. You should see `0` while QuickPizza is healthy, jumping above zero when 5xx errors happen in the last 5-minute window. If the preview is empty, double-check the data source, metric name, and label filter.
Your query now counts QuickPizza's 5xx errors over the last 5 minutes. In the next milestone, you set the condition that fires the alert the moment that count goes above zero.
